Subject: Post-demo: SLA-driven deployment path & GPU recommendation

Hi Samir — great demo earlier, thanks for walking us through Grainly's ingestion flow and realtime scoring use case. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can size a dedicated pool that meets your 95th-pct latency target.

Recap (what we heard):
- Workload: realtime scoring for customer chat and webhooks (inference on each message).
- Current expected steady-state: you mentioned a baseline of ~200 TPS, with traffic spikes up to ~450 TPS during peak windows.
- Latency target: 95th pct at or below ~150 ms end-to-end (model inference portion should be lower).
- Token mix: short prompts (system + message history) and longer generated completions for context-aware suggestions.

Asks (to confirm):
1) Can you confirm the steady-state and peak TPS numbers (200 / 450 above)?
2) Average prompt length and average generation length (tokens per request) — sample numbers are fine.
3) Any strict compliance requirements that force Private/VPC (SOC2 + customer contracts vs acceptable for Dedicated with VPC)?

Next steps I propose:
- You reply with the TPS and token averages.
- We'll run an initial dedicated-sizing worksheet (attached) and suggest an H100 vs A100 configuration with a recommended concurrency profile.
- If you need Private deployment, we'll list the minimal evidence items and timeline.

I've attached the lightweight sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx) and a one-page POC map (poc-map.png). Ben and Priyom are cc'd to add SE/ops guidance.

Thanks —

Thanks Camila — great summary. Confirming the numbers from our side after checking telemetry and product assumptions:

- Steady-state: ~210 TPS (this is what we see on average during business hours).
- Peak: short spikes up to ~480 TPS (multiple bursts of ~60–90s during batch imports and marketing windows).
- 95th-pct latency target: 150 ms end-to-end; model inference should aim for ~100 ms or less if possible.
- Token mix (approx per request):
  • prompt: 36 tokens (system + recent messages)
  • generation: ~190 tokens (summaries + suggestions)
  • total: ~226 tokens per request on average.

Security: most of our customers require SOC2 and IP protection. We prefer VPC/dedicated networking for production, but we can evaluate Dedicated with customer-managed VPC peering as an intermediate.

Happy to jump back on a quick 30-min sizing call next week if that helps.

—Samir

Thanks — adding SE recommendations and a pragmatic Dedicated sizing suggestion.

TL;DR recommendation: start Dedicated with an H100-optimized pool (quantized FP16/mixed-precision) sized to 4x H100-equivalents behind our autoscaler, with the following runtime knobs:
- target concurrency per GPU: tune to 8–12 concurrent requests for long-generation workloads (~200 tokens).
- batching: continuous batching with a max latency cap of 40 ms to preserve the 95th target.
- KV cache sizing: allocate per-GPU KV cache for 4k context; eviction policy LRU, warm-up via prefix caching for common system prompts.

Sizing math (back-of-envelope):
- average tokens/request: 226 → average generation higher compute cost than prompt.
- Steady 210 TPS * 226 tokens = ~47.5k tokens/sec.
- With aggressive quantization and optimized kernels H100 can handle ~12–18k gen-tokens/sec per card depending on model family; conservatively assume 13k gen-tokens/sec effective.
- 4x H100 => ~52k gen-tokens/sec effective → covers steady-state + buffer; autoscale adds 1–2 cards during sustained peaks toward 6 cards.

Operational notes:
- If Grainly requires strict customer-managed networking, Dedicated with VPC peering is the fastest path to production. Private/on-prem is a longer lead (4–8 weeks) and requires additional compliance paperwork.
- If end-to-end 95th-emphasis holds, we should plan canary rollouts and synthetic traffic for SLA verification (I can share a synthetic harness link).

Action items:
- Camila: share final signed M.A.P. and approve a 2-week POC window.
- Samir: confirm cost sensitivity / upper bound and whether you want us to price A100 vs H100 combo options.
- Priyom: I'll hand off the sizing workbook and an ops playbook for autoscaling triggers.
